title: Treasury International Capital (TIC) monthly release (August 2026 data) — the annual-revision edition, 4:00 p.m. ET
source: TSY: home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data, fetched direct by this event's own research session 2026-09-08 (plain curl, HTTP 200). The 2026 table's October row reads '16' in the Monthly column under the page header 'All data releases occur at 4 p.m. Washington, D.C. time'; the '30 - final' beside it is the annual SHCA report on U.S. portfolio holdings of foreign securities, a different series. Reference month August 2026 by the page's own 1.5-month lag rule. PROMOTED from estimate 2026-09-08 on the mts-october-2026-11-12 precedent (one named Treasury primary + independent mechanical corroboration, the no-self-confirm limit cleared because this event's OWN session re-fetched rather than the import-export/September sweep that discovered it). The mechanical corroboration is stronger here than the proposal's: the page's published '11th business day plus 0 to 3 days' rule, computed with federal holidays excluded (Columbus Day 10-12), puts the 11th business day of October 2026 on 2026-10-16 EXACTLY — offset +0, not merely inside the window. The same convention reproduces all 24 published 2026-27 dates to within the rule 22 times and hits 9 of them exactly, including the confirmed 2026-09-16; the weekday-only convention scores 20/24 and 5/24. Existence risk RETIRED, not assumed: the October 2025 TIC release was CANCELLED outright by the FY2026 lapse (Treasury's own sb0317, 2025-11-18, verbatim 'data for August (delayed by the partial shutdown of the federal government) and September 2025'), but PL 119-103 funds agencies through 2026-12-11, so 2026-10-16 sits inside a funded window. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: The calendar's only capital-account print, and — unlike its September sibling — on a date no Fed decision owns, which is why this entry exists. What makes it different in kind: October is one of the four ANNUAL-REVISION releases (Treasury's own note (c): 'The January, April, July, and October releases reflect revised data for the past year'), so the twelve months of history every model here is fitted on get restated on this date. Measured, not assumed: revision-month releases are the only TIC releases whose next session is NOT unusually quiet (mean |d10Y| 4.00bp on n=9 vs 2.55bp on the other 20, t=+2.13, p=0.033) — but still no noisier than an ordinary session (4.56bp), so the stand-aside holds. The reason to read it: August 2026's month-end 10Y was 4.75% against July's 4.75% — a Δ of ZERO, the third such month in 41 — so the mark-to-market wedge that dominated July (modelled ≈ −$95bn) vanishes and the model's prediction collapses to its intercept alone. That makes this the cleanest direct test of the valuation model in the series, and it makes August's headline holdings delta a near-clean read on flow rather than price. Impact LOW and symbols empty: 16:00 ET is after the equity cash close, the data is six weeks stale, and no house playbook is macro-keyed. Nothing here licenses an entry.
